queue_items.claim: The row names a byte-true cross-seam continuity fact as 'the seam's real warrant' for its own front cut, and no tier-1 onset class stands in its opening verse's bytes.
queue_items.grounds: boundary_rationale reads '...but the second-person plural ADDRESSEE carries across the seam: Isa.30.18’s object suffixes answer the same second-person plural running through Isa.30.15 and Isa.30.17. That addressee continuity, not a continuing speaking voice, is the seam’s real warrant.' The cited tokens are byte-true — גְּבֽוּרַתְכֶ֑ם and אֲבִיתֶֽם (oshb:Isa.30.15, byte tier), תָּנֻ֑סוּ and נוֹתַרְתֶּ֗ם (oshb:Isa.30.17, byte tier) — and the answering suffix stands inside the row's own opener וְלָכֵ֞ן יְחַכֶּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לַֽחֲנַנְכֶ֔ם (oshb:Isa.30.18, byte tier). A byte-true device straddling a row's own seam argues continuity AGAINST the cut; disclosing it is right, but it cannot be the cut's warrant. What the opening verse's own bytes carry is a consequence connector, a backward-linking particle, not a hoy, massa, divine frame, addressee shift, vocative or imperative onset; the row itself states the addressee does not shift. The tier-3 layer also does not sit at this seam: MT 30:17 carries no seg (chapter 30's segs are SAMEKH at MT 30:5, 30:11, 30:18, 30:26, 30:33 and PE at MT 30:14), so the nearest marked division, at MT 30:18, falls AFTER the row's own opening verse, interior to the span. No frame-onset deviation is registered and frontier_flag_considered is false, at confidence medium.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): restate the addressee continuity as the disclosed cross-seam cohesion it is, name the ground the onset verse's own bytes carry, and register the frame-onset deviation or lower the band. Disagreement with the row's stated grounds — routed onward, not adjudicated here.

queue_items.claim: The 25-verse digit belongs to the substring class that blends bare and waw-prefixed forms, not to 'the bare particle' the prose names; the bare particle stands at 23 verses, and the row's own onset is the waw-prefixed form.
queue_items.grounds: boundary_rationale reads 'the bare particle stands at exactly 25 verses book-wide at consonantal-skeleton tier and is the same connector, לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Isa.30.12, byte tier), that opens the indictment frame earlier in this chapter'. Re-swept: the contiguous skeleton substring returns exactly 25 MT verses, but a word-bound token split of the same hit set gives 23 verses carrying the bare form and 2 carrying the waw-prefixed form — MT 8:7 and MT 30:18, the row's own opening verse. The row's onset is וְלָכֵ֞ן יְחַכֶּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לַֽחֲנַנְכֶ֔ם (oshb:Isa.30.18, byte tier), waw-prefixed, while its comparator לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Isa.30.12, byte tier) is bare; the prefix difference is never disclosed, so a digit for one object is attached to prose naming another.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): either cite 23 verses for the bare particle and disclose that this row's own onset is the waw-prefixed form, or keep 25 and name the swept object as the skeleton class including waw-prefixed forms.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A consequence connector opens this row, וְלָכֵ֞ן יְחַכֶּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לַֽחֲנַנְכֶ֔ם (oshb:Isa.30.18, byte tier), the same particle recurring a second time later in the same verse; the bare particle stands at exactly 25 verses book-wide at consonantal-skeleton tier and is the same connector, לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Isa.30.12, byte tier), that opens the indictment frame earlier in this chapter, so the turn is argued as a consequence rather than a fresh temporal onset. “Therefore Yahweh will wait, that he may be gracious to you” (web:Isa.30.18) turns away from the flight-and-siege verdict closing at web:Isa.30.17. The speaker changes there -- divine first-person address under the frame at oshb:Isa.30.15 (גְּבֽוּרַתְכֶ֑ם, אֲבִיתֶֽם) and at oshb:Isa.30.17 (תָּנֻ֑סוּ, נוֹתַרְתֶּ֗ם) gives way to third-person report at Isa.30.18 -- but the second-person plural ADDRESSEE carries across the seam: Isa.30.18's object suffixes answer the same second-person plural running through Isa.30.15 and Isa.30.17. That addressee continuity, not a continuing speaking voice, is the seam's real warrant. The promise runs through restored teachers, rejected idols, and agricultural blessing without a further frame break, closing on “heals the wound they were struck with.” (web:Isa.30.26), the verse just before the theophany onset at web:Isa.30.27.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival cut would separate the graciousness promise (Isa.30.18-Isa.30.19) from the agricultural blessing (Isa.30.23-Isa.30.26) as two distinct oracles.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Zion promise oracle of grace, restored teachers, and agricultural abundance
shipped_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
shipped_row.device_notes: A paseq mark (single-witness) sits at oshb:Isa.30.25, inside the span, the next paseq site being Isa.31.4 beyond it; disclosed here, tallying presence rather than placement. Both the row's own opening verse Isa.30.18 and its closing verse Isa.30.26 carry a marked division, disclosed in its evidence refs.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A second-person command opens this row, עַתָּ֗ה בּ֣וֹא כָתְבָ֥הּ (oshb:Isa.30.8, byte tier), “Now go, write it before them on a tablet, and inscribe it in a book” (web:Isa.30.8), a commission addressed to the prophet himself rather than to the nation, distinct enough from the massa unit closing at web:Isa.30.7 to open a new row. Two divine frames follow inside this span: אֶת קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.30.11, byte tier), “Cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us.” (web:Isa.30.11); לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.30.12, byte tier), where the title itself is the frame owner since no adjacent divine name stands in the clause, “Therefore the Holy One of Israel says” (web:Isa.30.12); and כִּ֣י כֹֽה אָמַר֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֜ה קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Isa.30.15, byte tier), where the divine name stands inside the frame itself, “For thus said the Lord Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel” (web:Isa.30.15) -- both divine frames, so the koh-amar material at Isa.30.12 and Isa.30.15 is read as elaborating the same commissioned address rather than opening a fresh unit. It closes on “like a banner on a hill.” (web:Isa.30.17), the verse just before the reversal at web:Isa.30.18.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: An alternative opens a fresh row at the koh-amar formula of Isa.30.12 or Isa.30.15 rather than treating the whole tablet-commission passage as one unit.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: commission to record the people's rebellion on a tablet, with the rationale for judgment through a collapsing-wall image and refused rest
prev_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
prev_row.device_notes: The Holy One of Israel title recurs three times inside this row (Isa.30.11, Isa.30.12, Isa.30.15), read as texture supporting internal coherence rather than a boundary driver on its own -- correct against the 25-verse book-wide inventory, whose chapters-28-31 members are Isa.29.19, Isa.30.11, Isa.30.12, Isa.30.15, Isa.31.1. The row's two marked divisions -- a setumah at Isa.30.11, a distinct petuchah at Isa.30.14 -- are disclosed in its evidence refs. The onset עַתָּ֗ה בּ֣וֹא (oshb:Isa.30.8, byte tier) carries second-person masculine singular marking against the plural marking around it; the verse itself names no addressee, so the commission's assignment to the prophet is held as an inference rather than a claim the verse's own bytes carry.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A theophany closes this stretch of oracles, opening this row on הִנֵּ֤ה שֵׁם יְהוָה֙ בָּ֣א מִמֶּרְחָ֔ק (oshb:Isa.30.27, byte tier), “Behold, Yahweh’s name comes from far away, burning with his anger,” (web:Isa.30.27), a fresh onset after the blessing oracle closing at web:Isa.30.26. The same root answers itself at the row's own close: בֹּעֵ֣ר (oshb:Isa.30.27, byte tier) is picked up by בֹּעֲרָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.30.33, byte tier), a root-level inclusio running the row's own length across two distinct attested spellings. Isa.30.33 is itself a ketiv/qere-bearing verse; the row closes on “Yahweh’s breath, like a stream of sulfur, kindles it.” (web:Isa.30.33), quoted from its closing clause, after the varying token near that verse’s start.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: An alternative keeps this theophany inside the same row as the preceding blessing oracle rather than cutting at the fresh onset of Isa.30.27.
next_row.literature_type_guess: theophany oracle of Yahweh's judgment against Assyria, closing at the Topheth pyre image

next_row.device_notes: Both the row's front seam Isa.30.26 and its own closing verse Isa.30.33 carry a marked division, disclosed in its evidence refs; Isa.30.33's ketiv/qere note sits earlier in the verse than the quoted closing clause. A second variant note (single-witness apparatus) sits at oshb:Isa.30.32, disclosed here alongside the one at Isa.30.33, without adjudicating either reading. At the rear edge, an unpointed stem recurs: הֶעְמִ֣יק (oshb:Isa.30.33, byte tier) and its plural inflection הֶעְמִ֥יקוּ (oshb:Isa.31.6, byte tier), word-bound to the same root and attested at exactly 2 verses book-wide; a fresh hoy onset at oshb:Isa.31.1 carries the cut here, with the existing SAMEKH mark at oshb:Isa.30.33 corroborating at tier-3, and this catchword adds further corroboration rather than contesting either.

queue_items.claim: The 18-verse digit for the verse-initial presentative names no tier, holds only at skeleton tier, and its eighteenth member there is a ketiv token rather than the pointed presentative the row names; the pointed form stands verse-initial at 17.
queue_items.grounds: boundary_rationale reads 'The presentative הֵ֥ן opening this verse stands verse-initial at exactly 18 verses book-wide, only two of them in chapters 28-35'. Re-swept on first-token identity: 18 MT verses at consonantal-skeleton tier, 17 at accent-stripped tier. The skeleton-only member is MT 54:16, whose verse-initial token is the unpointed ketiv standing before its pointed qere; that verse is K/Q-bearing in the inventory, which is exactly the class the K/Q-before-counting rule guards. The row's own splice is the pointed form הֵ֥ן (oshb:Isa.32.1, byte tier, re-collated). The dependent sub-claim survives: at both tiers the only chs 28-35 members are MT 32:1 and MT 33:7.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): cite 17 verses at accent-stripped tier for the pointed presentative, or keep 18 while naming the skeleton tier and disclosing the MT 54:16 ketiv member.

queue_items.claim: device_notes lists a parashah mark as one of the three grounds the boundary rests on; in the Prophets the layer is tier-3 weak corroboration and never a boundary driver.
queue_items.grounds: device_notes reads 'resting the boundary on the fresh subject (the coming king), the verse-initial presentative, and the parashah PE mark at oshb:Isa.32.8.' The mark is real and correctly typed — PE at MT 32:8, not conflated with the SAMEKH segs at MT 31:9 and MT 32:20 — and it is disclosed single-witness, but 'resting the boundary on' it makes a tier-3 signal load-bearing. The row's boundary_rationale keeps the same mark to the corroboration side ('corroborating the break'), so the two fields do not describe the mark's weight the same way.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): restate the PE as tier-3 corroboration of the rear seam and remove it from the list of grounds the boundary rests on.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: This unit opens at הֵ֥ן לְצֶ֖דֶק יִמְלָךְ מֶ֑לֶךְ וּלְשָׂרִ֖ים לְמִשְׁפָּ֥ט יָשֹֽׂרוּ (oshb:Isa.32.1, byte tier), “Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in justice.” (web:Isa.32.1), a fresh topic onset describing a future righteous ruler; the closing signature at oshb:Isa.31.9 does not carry its own addressee forward into this new topic. The presentative הֵ֥ן opening this verse stands verse-initial at exactly 18 verses book-wide, only two of them in chapters 28-35 -- this site and oshb:Isa.33.7 -- so the particle alone does not discriminate the two; what distinguishes this site is the topic itself, a coming king unconnected to anything preceding it, where the parallel site continues describing an already-open scene rather than opening one. The span continues describing the ruler's effect and the noble-versus-scoundrel contrast through oshb:Isa.32.8 and closes there, immediately before the vocative onset that opens the following unit at oshb:Isa.32.9, “Rise up, you women who are at ease! Hear my voice!” oshb:Isa.31.9, the verse immediately ahead of this unit's own onset, is closed by a parashah SAMEKH mark (single-witness); at the unit's own close, oshb:Isa.32.8 carries a parashah PE mark (single-witness) corroborating the break.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A split at web:Isa.32.5, where the description sharpens from noble rule in general to the fool-and-scoundrel contrast in particular, found no support: no addressee or frame shift accompanies that sharpening, and the passage continues describing the same righteous order through web:Isa.32.8.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: oracle of a future righteous king and his officials

shipped_row.device_notes: The unit is bounded by topic onset rather than a hoy or massa marker; this row registers that deviation from the frame-onset default per the operative-category allowance, resting the boundary on the fresh subject (the coming king), the verse-initial presentative, and the parashah PE mark at oshb:Isa.32.8. A variant note (single-witness apparatus) sits at oshb:Isa.32.7, disclosed here without adjudicating the reading; the row neither quotes nor slices that verse.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: This unit opens at the hoy onset web:Isa.31.1, “Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, and rely on horses, and trust in chariots because they are many, and in horsemen because they are very strong, but they don't look to the Holy One of Israel, and they don't seek Yahweh!”, pointed ה֣וֹי הַיֹּרְדִ֤ים מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לְעֶזְרָ֔ה עַל סוּסִ֖ים יִשָּׁעֵ֑נוּ וַיִּבְטְח֨וּ עַל רֶ֜כֶב כִּ֣י רָ֗ב וְעַ֤ל פָּֽרָשִׁים֙ כִּֽי עָצְמ֣וּ מְאֹ֔ד וְלֹ֤א שָׁעוּ֙ עַל קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאֶת יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֥א דָרָֽשׁוּ (oshb:Isa.31.1, tier: byte), which names the qadosh-Israel title inside the woe clause itself. A divine-frame formula opens a first-person Yahweh word within the same complex at oshb:Isa.31.4, כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָֽמַר יְהוָ֣ה אֵלַ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶהְגֶּה֩ הָאַרְיֵ֨ה וְהַכְּפִ֜יר עַל טַרְפּ֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִקָּרֵ֤א עָלָיו֙ מְלֹ֣א רֹעִ֔ים מִקּוֹלָם֙ לֹ֣א יֵחָ֔ת וּמֵֽהֲמוֹנָ֖ם לֹ֣א יַֽעֲנֶ֑ה כֵּ֗ן יֵרֵד֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת לִצְבֹּ֥א עַל הַר צִיּ֖וֹן וְעַל גִּבְעָתָֽהּ (tier: byte), and the span closes with a postpositive signature at oshb:Isa.31.9, וְסַלְעוֹ֙ מִמָּג֣וֹר יַֽעֲב֔וֹר וְחַתּ֥וּ מִנֵּ֖ס שָׂרָ֑יו נְאֻם יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁר א֥וּר לוֹ֙ בְּצִיּ֔וֹן וְתַנּ֥וּר ל֖וֹ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם (tier: byte), bracketing the whole hoy-framed span. Just ahead of this unit's onset, oshb:Isa.30.33 carries a parashah SAMEKH mark (single-witness); two further SAMEKH marks (single-witness), at oshb:Isa.31.3 and oshb:Isa.31.9, are also disclosed, the latter coinciding with the unit's own closing signature. An imperative address opens at שׁ֗וּבוּ לַאֲשֶׁ֛ר הֶעְמִ֥יקוּ סָרָ֖ה בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.31.6, byte tier), “Return to him from whom you have deeply revolted, children of Israel.” (web:Isa.31.6), and the Assyrian's downfall follows at web:Isa.31.8-Isa.31.9 as internal texture within the same bracketed complex, carrying a fresh addressee shift but not a fresh hoy, massa, or divine-frame marker of its own. This same verb recurs at the row's own front seam: הֶעְמִ֥יקוּ shares its unpointed stem with הֶעְמִ֣יק closing oshb:Isa.30.33 (byte tier; that verse's own ketiv/qere variance sits earlier in it, outside the quoted word), word-bound to the same root and attested at exactly 2 verses book-wide -- corroborating, not contesting, the hoy onset that opens this unit.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A split at web:Isa.31.6, where the imperative address to the returning children of Israel begins, was weighed and declined: that address introduces no hoy, massa, or new divine-frame marker of its own, and the postpositive signature at oshb:Isa.31.9 closes the whole complex as one bracketed unit.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: woe oracle against reliance on Egypt, incorporating a divine-word simile and a call to return

prev_row.device_notes: The imperative shift at web:Isa.31.6 and the Assyria-judgment turn at web:Isa.31.8 are registered as internal texture within the hoy-framed complex, not as separate frames. A paseq mark (single-witness) sits at oshb:Isa.31.4 inside the divine-frame clause, tallying presence rather than placement. This span covers the whole of chapter 31 (9 verses, per the book's verse inventory); its confidence is held at medium_low under the campaign's whole-chapter ceiling, a calibration cap rather than a newly found defect in the row's evidence.

next_row.boundary_rationale: This unit opens at the vocative address נָשִׁים֙ שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת קֹ֖מְנָה שְׁמַ֣עְנָה קוֹלִ֑י (oshb:Isa.32.9, byte tier), “Rise up, you women who are at ease! Hear my voice!” (web:Isa.32.9), a direct imperative address distinct from the third-person description of web:Isa.32.1-Isa.32.8, repeated in the same terms at web:Isa.32.11. Isa.32.15's subordinating opener, עַד יֵ֨עָרֶ֥ה עָלֵ֛ינוּ ר֖וּחַ מִמָּר֑וֹם (oshb:Isa.32.15, byte tier; this verse's ketiv/qere note falls later in it, outside the quoted span), does not open a fresh clause but continues the sentence begun in the desolation description of Isa.32.14, and its resolution is picked up by the waw-plus-perfect וְשָׁכַ֥ן בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר מִשְׁפָּ֑ט (oshb:Isa.32.16, byte tier) in the identical construction: nothing verse-initial marks a fresh start at Isa.32.16, and the English adverb rendering that verse's opening renders this waw form rather than a distinct Hebrew adverb, אָ֥ז (oshb:Isa.35.5, byte tier), which stands verse-initial at exactly six sites book-wide at accent-stripped tier (oshb:Isa.35.5, oshb:Isa.35.6, oshb:Isa.58.8, oshb:Isa.58.9, oshb:Isa.58.14, oshb:Isa.60.5), none of them this verse. This clause chain is what withdraws any seam between Isa.32.15 and Isa.32.16 and keeps the restoration announced there inside the same address rather than opening a fresh unit. The unit runs on through the peaceful-dwelling and beatitude material, closing on אַשְׁרֵיכֶ֕ם (oshb:Isa.32.20, byte tier), “Blessed are you who sow beside all waters, who send out the feet of the ox and the donkey.” (web:Isa.32.20), immediately before the woe header ה֣וֹי שׁוֹדֵ֗ד (oshb:Isa.33.1, byte tier) that opens the following unit. A parashah PE mark (single-witness) closes at oshb:Isa.32.8 immediately before this unit's onset.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival cut would open a fresh unit at Isa.32.16, treating עַד יֵ֨עָרֶ֥ה (oshb:Isa.32.15, its own ketiv/qere note falling later in the verse than this quoted opener) as closing the preceding address and וְשָׁכַ֥ן בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר מִשְׁפָּ֑ט (oshb:Isa.32.16) as opening a fresh third-person description; it is declined because the two verses continue one waw-plus-perfect clause chain with nothing verse-initial marking a fresh start, and because both the at-ease catchword bracket and the trust-root answer named above run past that point to Isa.32.18, arguing for one span rather than two.
next_row.literature_type_guess: vocative judgment address to complacent women, closing in a temporal turn toward restoration
next_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
next_row.device_notes: A catchword bracket runs the length of the span: שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.32.9, byte tier) is byte-identical to שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.32.11, byte tier), and שַׁאֲנַנּֽוֹת (oshb:Isa.32.18, byte tier as spliced) joins them at consonantal-skeleton tier only, the three standing at exactly 3 verses book-wide at that tier and nowhere else in the book. A second bracket answers on the same root at a different grade: מִבְטַחִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.32.18, byte tier), attested at exactly 1 verse book-wide, answers בֹּֽטח֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.32.9, byte tier), that spelling standing at exactly 3 verses book-wide at consonantal-skeleton tier -- a root-level relation across two distinct attested spellings, not a token match. A ketiv/qere note (single-witness apparatus) sits at oshb:Isa.32.15, inside the internal clause chain; this row discloses the note without adjudicating the reading. The parashah PE at oshb:Isa.32.8 and the parashah SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.32.20 (both single-witness) corroborate the two outer seams alone, tier-3 and non-driving. This span carries a vocative judgment address at its onset governing the whole unit; the restoration promised from Isa.32.15 arrives as the resolution of that address's own subordinate clause rather than as a fresh salvation frame, and the unit closes in a beatitude -- an operative-category deviation disclosed here per the closed vocabulary's own rule, since judgment_oracle governs the span's own bytes from onset to close. The referent of the outpoured Spirit at Isa.32.15 remains a live construal question this row does not settle.

queue_items.claim: The row declines an interior seam at MT 33:13 on a stated rule that counts only hoy, massa and divine-frame markers, omitting the imperative-onset and addressee-shift class the tier-1 catalogue carries; its paired mark claim is byte-false at that very site, and the rule as stated is incompatible with the neighbouring unit's own onset.
queue_items.grounds: boundary_rationale quotes the verse-initial summons שִׁמְע֥וּ רְחוֹקִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתִי (oshb:Isa.33.13, byte tier, re-collated), an imperative with named addressees, and its two digits re-verify exactly — verse-initial at 10 MT verses book-wide (MT 1:2, 1:10, 33:13, 46:3, 46:12, 48:1, 49:1, 51:1, 51:7, 66:5) and at this single site across chs 28-35. It then declines the site because 'none carries a fresh hoy, massa, or divine-frame marker of its own; it is that absence ... that keeps the complex bounded as one unit'. Two things cut against that. First, the row's next sentence says the SAMEKH segs at MT 33:6 and MT 33:12 mark 'internal stanza turns that bind to no fresh hoy or vocative marker of their own'; that is true at MT 33:6, whose following verse opens on the presentative הֵ֚ן אֶרְאֶלָּ֔ם (oshb:Isa.33.7, byte tier), but false at MT 33:12, whose division falls immediately before the summons the row itself quotes — so the tier-3 layer's own division does bind to a fresh vocative-imperative marker there. queue_items.claim: The row's own onset verse carries no pointed splice, no tier label and no oshb: ref, and the rationale explicitly rests the seam on an audience question 'rather than on a new speech frame' although web:Isa.36.11 opens with exactly such a frame.
queue_items.grounds: oshb:Isa.36.11 opens וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶלְיָקִים֩ וְשֶׁבְנָ֨א וְיוֹאָ֜ח אֶל רַב שָׁקֵ֗ה (oshb:Isa.36.11, tier: byte) — a verse-initial vayomer with a full speaker-and-addressee inversion (the three officials now speak, the Rabshakeh is now addressed), the ruled tier-1 addressee/scene-shift signal for this seam. The row instead argues 'This short unit turns on an audience question rather than on a new speech frame', quotes only WEB for that verse, splices Hebrew only at oshb:Isa.36.12, and lists no oshb:Isa.36.11 in boundary_evidence_refs. The adopted bound is materially right; the stated warrant is weaker than, and contradicts, the row's own onset bytes. Everything else re-swept in this row holds: the bare hiriq-pointed adonai census is exactly three verses (word-bound sweep of the pointed forms at MT 36:8, 36:9, 36:12), the two adonai-family forms in 36:12 are distinct at byte and at finals-normalized skeleton tier, and the doubled ketiv/qere at 36:12 matches the single-witness inventory (two notes).
queue_items.proposed_change: In boundary_rationale, replace 'turns on an audience question rather than on a new speech frame' with a byte-grounded onset warrant — the verse-initial speech frame with speaker-and-addressee inversion, spliced as 'וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶלְיָקִים֩ וְשֶׁבְנָ֨א וְיוֹאָ֜ח אֶל רַב שָׁקֵ֗ה (oshb:Isa.36.11, tier: byte)' — keeping the audience question as the scene rationale, and add 'oshb:Isa.36.11' to boundary_evidence_refs. Span unchanged.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: This short unit turns on an audience question rather than on a new speech frame: at web:Isa.36.11, “Then Eliakim, Shebna and Joah said to Rabshakeh, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. Don’t speak to us in the Jews’ language in the hearing of the people who are on the wall.”” (web:Isa.36.11), the officials ask the Rabshakeh to switch languages so the people on the wall cannot follow; the request for Aramaic is narrated STORY CONTENT here, not a label on the verse's own language, which remains Hebrew throughout the staged extract. The Rabshakeh's refusal follows at web:Isa.36.12, “But Rabshakeh said, “Has my master sent me only to your master and to you, to speak these words, and not to the men who sit on the wall, who will eat their own dung and drink their own urine with you?”” (web:Isa.36.12), in Hebrew וַיֹּ֣אמֶר רַב שָׁקֵ֗ה הַאֶ֨ל אֲדֹנֶ֤יךָ וְאֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי אֲדֹנִ֔י לְדַבֵּ֖ר אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה הֲלֹ֣א עַל הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ עַל הַ֣חוֹמָ֔ה לֶאֱכֹ֣ל אֶת חראיהם צוֹאָתָ֗ם וְלִשְׁתּ֛וֹת אֶת שיניהם מֵימֵ֥י רַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם עִמָּכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.36.12, tier: byte), itself a doubled ketiv/qere verse (single-witness apparatus) and the site where the Rabshakeh's own title again surfaces as two separate tokens rather than one compound word, visible in the same pointed quote above. The same verse carries two distinct adonai-family forms rather than one form repeated: the second-person-singular-suffixed אֲדֹנֶ֤יךָ (oshb:Isa.36.12, tier: byte) and the first-person-singular-suffixed אֲדֹנִ֔י (oshb:Isa.36.12, tier: byte), distinct from each other at byte tier and at finals-normalized skeleton tier alike; only the second is a member of the book's bare hiriq-pointed adonai census, which stands at exactly three verses (MT 36:8, 36:9, 36:12). Both tokens name the human master relation rather than the divine title. This row closes with the Rabshakeh's own crude threat, before he turns to address the wider audience directly in the next unit.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: An alternative fold of this two-verse exchange into the surrounding Rabshakeh speech does not hold: the delegates' own request and the Rabshakeh's refusal turn on the audience question itself, a scene concern distinct from either flanking taunt. The frame-plus-speech default would instead keep the whole 36:4-20 complex as one continuous royal-messenger unit, an architecture this row's own addressee-question boundary argues against.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: the delegates' Aramaic request and the Rabshakeh's crude refusal before the wall
shipped_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
shipped_row.device_notes: Two ketiv/qere notes sit at oshb:Isa.36.12 (single-witness apparatus, the book's doubled-note class): the unpointed ketiv חראיהם pairs with the pointed qere צוֹאָתָ֗ם (oshb:Isa.36.12, tier: byte), and the unpointed ketiv שיניהם pairs with the pointed qere מֵימֵ֥י רַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם (oshb:Isa.36.12, tier: byte); both are disclosed as single-witness apparatus, never as boundary evidence. The Rabshakeh's own title, quoted in full at oshb:Isa.36.12 above, is confirmed as two separate tokens rather than a single compound word in the staged extract, and the Aramaic request is disclosed as narrated content about a language choice, never as a language label on the verse itself.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The Rabshakeh's own taunt opens this unit at web:Isa.36.4, “Rabshakeh said to them, “Now tell Hezekiah, ‘The great king, the king of Assyria, says, “What confidence is this in which you trust?”” (web:Isa.36.4), pointed as וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ רַב שָׁקֵ֔ה אִמְרוּ נָ֖א אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר מָ֧ה הַבִּטָּח֛וֹן הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּטָֽחְתָּ (oshb:Isa.36.4, tier: byte). The royal-messenger formula opening that verse belongs to the king of Assyria, not to Yahweh: the Rabshakeh speaks as his master's herald, and this row treats the whole taunt he delivers to the officials, through its own rhetorical close at web:Isa.36.10, “Have I come up now without Yahweh against this land to destroy it? Yahweh said to me, “Go up against this land, and destroy it.”””” (web:Isa.36.10), as one continuous speech act under that single royal frame. Mid-span, the Rabshakeh's own offer at web:Isa.36.8 names his master with the courtly sense of adoni, וְעַתָּה֙ הִתְעָ֣רֶב נָ֔א אֶת אֲדֹנִ֖י הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וְאֶתְּנָ֤ה לְךָ֙ אַלְפַּ֣יִם סוּסִ֔ים אִם תּוּכַ֕ל לָ֥תֶת לְךָ֖ רֹכְבִ֥ים עֲלֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Isa.36.8, tier: byte); the closing token there shares its consonantal skeleton — skeleton tier only — with the bare-adonai form that elsewhere in the book addresses the divine Adonai, though the pointing differs: hiriq here against the qamats that marks the divine title, and the referent is plainly the earthly king of Assyria, argued from the parallel 'my master the king of Assyria' in the same clause. This unit's own close at web:Isa.36.10 carries a further instance of the same construction, this time a YHWH-speech attribution placed inside the herald's own mouth, יְהוָה֙ אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Isa.36.10, tier: byte); the verse is absent from the book's amar/vayomer-plus-YHWH adjacency census (52 verses), and the word attributed to Yahweh here is the herald's own claim rather than a narrated speech event of Yahweh's own.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading web:Isa.36.4-Isa.36.20 as a single unbroken speech was weighed against this row's own bounds and rejected, since the delegates' own intervening request for Aramaic at web:Isa.36.11 marks a scene turn that this unit's own opening taunt does not itself carry.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: the Rabshakeh's opening taunt to Hezekiah's delegates, staged as the Assyrian king's own royal-messenger word
prev_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
prev_row.device_notes: The royal-messenger frame here belongs to the Assyrian king throughout, never to Yahweh; the bare-adonai token at web:Isa.36.8 carries the courtly 'my master' sense rather than the divine address the same consonants carry elsewhere in the book, a role split this row names rather than assumes. The same hiriq-pointed form recurs later in this unit at web:Isa.36.9, עַבְדֵ֥י אֲדֹנִ֖י (oshb:Isa.36.9, tier: byte), where the Rabshakeh again styles his own king as 'my master' before the lesser officials he addresses, completing the courtly-adonai disclosure across the whole span rather than at the one site.

next_row.boundary_rationale: This unit opens at web:Isa.36.13, “Then Rabshakeh stood, and called out with a loud voice in the Jews’ language, and said, “Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!”” (web:Isa.36.13), pointed at its onset as וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ רַב שָׁקֵ֔ה וַיִּקְרָ֥א בְקוֹל גָּד֖וֹל יְהוּדִ֑ית (oshb:Isa.36.13, tier: byte). The proclamation is made in a loud voice and in יְהוּדִ֑ית (oshb:Isa.36.13, tier: byte), the Judahite-language noun the verse itself carries, rather than the Aramaic the officials had just requested as narrated story content in the preceding unit; neither witness labels this proclamation 'Hebrew'. A second royal-messenger formula opens immediately at web:Isa.36.14, “The king says, ‘Don’t let Hezekiah deceive you; for he will not be able to deliver you.” (web:Isa.36.14), in Hebrew כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אַל יַשִּׁ֥א לָכֶ֖ם חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ כִּ֥י לֹֽא יוּכַ֖ל לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶתְכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.36.14, tier: byte), and a third opens at web:Isa.36.16, “Don’t listen to Hezekiah, for the king of Assyria says, ‘Make your peace with me, and come out to me; and each of you eat from his vine, and each one from his fig tree, and each one of you drink the waters of his own cistern;” (web:Isa.36.16), in Hebrew אַֽל תִּשְׁמְע֖וּ אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֗וּר עֲשֽׂוּ אִתִּ֤י בְרָכָה֙ וּצְא֣וּ אֵלַ֔י וְאִכְל֤וּ אִישׁ גַּפְנוֹ֙ וְאִ֣ישׁ תְּאֵנָת֔וֹ וּשְׁת֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ מֵי בוֹרֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.36.16, tier: byte), both still spoken under the Assyrian king's own frame rather than Yahweh's; this same verse also carries a parashah SAMEKH mark (single-witness), oshb:Isa.36.16. The unit runs to its own rhetorical climax at web:Isa.36.20, “Who are they among all the gods of these countries that have delivered their country out of my hand, that Yahweh should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?’”” (web:Isa.36.20), before the officials' silence closes the scene in the following unit.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: web:Isa.36.13-Isa.36.20 could instead be read as a continuation of the same speech unit that opens at web:Isa.36.4, but the intervening audience exchange and the switch to a public proclamation before the people on the wall argue against that, marking a fresh address of a different audience under a restated frame.
next_row.literature_type_guess: the Rabshakeh's public Hebrew proclamation to the people on the wall, a renewed royal-messenger taunt
next_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
next_row.device_notes: Both koh-amar onsets inside this unit (36:14, 36:16) belong to the Assyrian king's own herald frame, restated for the new audience on the wall rather than opening any divine word; the parashah mark at 36:16 falls mid-speech and is disclosed here without being read as a structural break inside the Rabshakeh's own continuous address.
